correctness.rationale: For m>=2, the cocktail-party graph K_{2m} minus a fixed perfect matching has local closed-neighborhood rule based on total ones S minus the chosen mate bit. With k mixed deleted-matching pairs, cut c=m^2-(S-m)^2-k, which never decreases under the strict minority move. Reach S=m using allowed updates, then consume two mixed pairs via a two-step path until maximal cut; this gives finite positive-probability access from every state to the recurrent maximum-cut locus. Even m gives exactly C(m,m/2) absorbing homogeneous configurations. Odd m gives (m+3)C(m,(m-1)/2) configurations in one reversible communicating class; the transition graph is the doubled-edge subdivision of the connected middle-two-rank inclusion graph. Its Laplacian BB^T=2(dI+A_H) has least positive eigenvalue d+1-sqrt((d+1)^2-2), and each edge transition has rate 1/(2m), proving the exact gap. Independent literal full-transition SCC census m=2,3,4,5 matches populations and the odd-m spectral gaps.

originality.rationale: The original Regnault–Rouquier–Thierry fully asynchronous minority work defines the same update, potential and general cut-energy monotonicity and studies complete cliques, trees, paths, grids and bipartite graphs, not deletion of a full perfect matching and the resulting one-class odd-m subdivision spectrum. Published complete split-graph minority analysis has a structurally different graph and spectral gap 1/(a+b), not this shrinking ~m^-2 gap. Classical middle-level inclusion graph eigenvalues are honestly used as input. No exact matching dynamic classification or dominating theorem identified.
residual_risks: An unindexed zero-temperature anti-coordination process on cocktail-party graphs may have established the same attractors under alternate graph nomenclature.

value.rationale: The natural perfect-matching deletion of a clique changes the terminal stochastic-minority attractor type dramatically with the number of pairs: absorbing combinatorial family versus a connected nonabsorbing class. Its exact mixing spectral gap and doubled-subdivision representation are substantive dynamics and spectral graph information, not a textbook application once the recurrent configuration graph is identified.

limitations: No exact absorption time or worst-case total variation mixing time from arbitrary initial states.
The spectral-gap assertion applies to the unique odd-m recurrent chain, not to the even-m reducible full chain.
